Anna — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below, plus a proposed next step (kickoff + evidence mapping call).

Quick status summary:
- ISO 27001: We completed an internal gap analysis (v0.3) in Nov 2025; scope includes platform services and the hosted API. We have a remediation backlog and believe external certification is achievable in H3 2026 assuming prioritized remediation.
- FedRAMP (moderate): No formal FedRAMP assessments yet. We have a mapping to NIST SP 800-53 controls and a plan to pursue readiness assessment in H2 2026. Achieving an Authority to Operate (ATO) will likely extend beyond one year and depends on a sponsoring agency.
- Artifacts: We can provide policies (ISMS, access control, incident response), system diagrams, network segmentation doc, encryption at rest/in transit details, and preliminary SOC 2 evidence packages for several control families. Some artifact generation (e.g., configuration snapshots, runtime logs with retention) will require 1–4 weeks to collect.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kickoff call with Acme sec team (30–45 min) to confirm scope & prioritization — can you do Tue Jan 20 or Wed Jan 21?
2) I will attach our preliminary checklist and the gap analysis PDF for your review (attached).
3) If you can send a prioritized control list (e.g., AC, IA, CM), we will provide estimated delivery dates per artifact.

Internal owners (for your reference):
- Soojin Lee — compliance lead (this thread owner)
- Rishi Malhotra — security engineering (evidence collection / configuration)
- Grace O'Connor — GRC advisor (policy / audit readiness)

I attached: redwood_compliance_prelim_checklist.pdf and redwood_iso_gap_analysis_v0.3.pdf.

Thanks — I'll hold off on any large evidence pulls until we confirm what you need during the kickoff.

Hi Anna / team — looping in a more detailed breakdown and realistic internal ETA estimates.

Short answers first:
- ISO external audit target: aiming to schedule auditor engagement in Aug 2026, external audit Sep 2026 (paperwork and remediation dependent).
- FedRAMP readiness assessment: target readiness assessment window May–Jun 2026; actual ATO timeline will depend on sponsor agency + 3PAO findings.

Artifact ETA (by control family, approximate):
- Policies (ISMS, IR, BC/DR): AVAILABLE NOW (policies are finalized and attached to the Drive link).
- System/network diagrams, data flow: 1 week to produce current diagrams (we have drafts).
- Configuration snapshots (IAM roles, VPC configs): 2–3 weeks (requires export & review).
- Runtime logs / monitoring evidence (SI): 4–6 weeks (may require short-term retention adjustments).
- Pen test reports / vuln scans: we have a quarterly scan; pen test schedule Q2 2026.

Practical constraints: some items (evidence exports, legal review for disclosures) require coordination with product engineering and infra ops. To keep turnaround under 3 weeks for most requests, we suggest a prioritized list from Acme (top 10 controls).

We've created a Jira ticket to track evidence requests: SEC-1123 (linked). I've attached a FedRAMP-to-NIST mapping workbook (fedramp_mapping_v1.xlsx) which has our initial control mapping.

I'll be on the Jan 20 call; proposed agenda:
1) Confirm scope (ISO only vs ISO + FedRAMP)
2) Prioritize control families and artifact list
3) Agree on timelines and owner assignments
4) Next steps & hubspot/opportunity expectations (HUB-78921)
